# pulse_sso_mapping (Resource)

Grants a dashboard role to everyone who signs in through an SSO provider while in a given group. The provider's `groups_claim` names the ID token claim that lists the person's groups; at each SSO sign-in Pulse replaces the user's SSO roles with the roles of every mapping that matches. These roles show up in `pulse_user.sso_roles`, never in `pulse_user.roles`.

Removing a mapping takes the role away at the user's next SSO sign-in. Map several groups or roles with several mappings; the same group and role can be mapped only once per provider.

Import with `<provider_id>/<mapping_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Members of the "pulse-admins" group get the administrator role, "pulse-ops" the operator role.
resource "pulse_sso_mapping" "admins" {
  provider_id = pulse_sso_provider.keycloak.id
  group_value = "pulse-admins"
  role        = "administrator"
}

resource "pulse_sso_mapping" "ops" {
  provider_id = pulse_sso_provider.keycloak.id
  group_value = "pulse-ops"
  role        = "operator"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_value` (String) A value of the provider's groups claim, exactly as the provider sends it (a group name or, for Microsoft Entra ID, a group object ID; at most 256 bytes). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `provider_id` (String) ID of the SSO provider (`pulse_sso_provider.<name>.id`). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `role` (String) Role granted: `administrator`, `operator`, `auditor`, `viewer`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Mapping ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <provider_id>/<mapping_id>
terraform import pulse_sso_mapping.admins 01j9z6t0b1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9/01j9z6w2c3d4e5f6g7h8j9k0m1
```
